title: Four squares in caps, and Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of two results on sums of four squares. (1) Jacobi's four-square theorem for odd N: the number of x : Fin 4 → ℤ with x₀² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃² = N equals 8 ∑_{d ∣ N} d (jacobi_four_squares_odd), following the proof of Andrews, Ekhad and Zeilberger (1993): two finite q-series identities proved by WZ telescoping, combined into a finite identity that is read modulo X^{N+1} in ℚ⟦X⟧. (2) Four squares in caps (four_squares_in_caps): for every unit vector q ∈ ℝ⁴ and every δ > 0 there is M₀ such that every odd m ≥ M₀ is β₀² + β₁² + β₂² + β₃² with β : Fin 4 → ℤ and |βᵢ − √m qᵢ| ≤ δ √m for all i, i.e. the integer points of the sphere of radius √m meet every cap of fixed angular radius. The proof uses the Duke–Friedlander–Iwaniec delta method (in Heath-Brown's form) with Gaussian weights: an exact formula through the theta transformation, Fourier bounds for the cut-off weight, and the Weil bound for Kloosterman sums, imported from the Weil Bounds Toolkit (PALOMAR-2026-11-03-000018) as a lake dependency. The main term is not evaluated: it depends on the center of the cap only through its norm, so comparing caps with a grid of centers reduces the theorem to the lower bound r₄(m) ≥ 8m for odd m, which (1) provides. All constants are effective but not explicit in the statement (M₀ is existential). Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.
